app_info.subtitle: See which devices pass checks
app_info.description:
Ask about the devices in your XFA organization: which ones pass their security checks, which need fixing, and how that changes over time, for example before an audit or a customer security review. XFA is user-driven device security that keeps work moving, for fast-growing tech companies, often without an IT team. It checks the security of every device when someone signs in to work apps, on company-issued, personal and contractor laptops and phones, and warns people first. It takes no control of the device. People install the XFA app themselves at their first sign-in, and when a check fails they fix it themselves, with the Fix button where XFA offers one or a step by step guide. XFA also finds devices through your identity provider. This connector lets the assistant read those results. It cannot change anything.

What you can ask:
- Which devices do not meet our policy, and what fails on each?
- Which devices have an out of date operating system, or disk encryption off?
- What do jane@example.com's devices look like?
- How many people still have no verified device?
- Which checks does our policy require, and which only warn?
- Which devices are affected by a given CVE?
- How has disk encryption changed over the last 90 days?

Intended users: admins and security or IT leads of an organization that uses XFA, who want answers about their devices without opening the dashboard, for example to prepare an audit or follow up on a vulnerability. A person connects with their own XFA account, and sees what their role in each organization allows in the dashboard.

What it reads:
- Per device: the email of the person who uses it, their name and the computer's name where known, the make and model, the operating system and its version, the browser and its version, and which of them are up to date.
- Per device check results, for example disk encryption, screen lock, firewall, antivirus, password manager and remote access settings, plus the versions of common work apps such as Slack, Zoom and Microsoft Office.
- Whether the device meets your policy, whether it is verified (checked directly by XFA, usually through the XFA app) or only discovered through your identity provider, and the tags and notes your admins gave it.
- On request, the known vulnerabilities (CVE ids) of a device's operating system and browser.
- Your policies, with the checks each one requires and whether a failing check warns or blocks a sign-in.
- Your organization's name, contact details, settings and plan features, and who you are in XFA with your role.
- Company-wide figures, such as how many devices and people are verified or compliant, and the same figures day by day.
- Looking up a software version or its vulnerabilities on its own says nothing about your devices. Vulnerabilities of your devices come with the device results.

Limits:
- Read-only. It cannot change settings, policies, tags or devices, and it cannot start a fix. People fix their own devices in the XFA app.
- Only the organizations you approve when you connect. It reads one organization at a time.
- Counts of devices and people in the company-wide figures cover the last 30 days. Device lists follow the dashboard's 30 days unless you ask for another period.
- A day by day look covers 30 days at a time, so a longer period takes several steps.
- Discovered devices show less than verified ones, and some details depend on your plan. A missing check means unknown, not failing.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves the caller's XFA organization details and does not modify data.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads only the organization's private XFA data and does not write to the public internet or third-party systems.

test_cases.description: Identify the organization the user is connected to.
test_cases.user_prompt: What organization am I connected to in XFA?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the name and key details of the organization the signed-in user approved.

test_cases.description: Summarize device compliance for the organization.
test_cases.user_prompt: How many of our devices are non-compliant right now?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a compliance summary with compliant vs non-compliant device counts.

test_cases.user_prompt: List our devices that were active in the last 30 days.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the organization's recently active devices with their check results.

test_cases.user_prompt: What do jane@example.com's devices look like?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the devices of that person with their check results.

test_cases.user_prompt: Which security policies do we have configured?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the list of policies configured for the organization.

test_cases.description: Check known vulnerabilities for a software version.
test_cases.user_prompt: Are there known CVEs for Google Chrome 120?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the CVEs XFA tracks for that software version, if any.

test_cases.user_prompt: Which groups of devices do we have?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the tags administrators gave the organization's devices.

test_cases.description: Show how a policy treats failing checks.
test_cases.user_prompt: Which checks does our policy require, and which only warn?
test_cases.expected_output: Returns each policy's rules: which checks are on and whether a failing check warns or blocks a sign-in.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not attempt destructive device actions.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Delete the laptop belonging to john@example.com.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it is read-only and cannot delete or change devices.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not attempt enrollment or write actions.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Enroll a new device into our organization.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because it cannot create or modify records.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for unrelated requests.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What's the weather in Brussels today?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the request is outside its device security questions.
